title: S. cerevisiae Microbial Community Alterations and Correlations
summary: This cluster revolves around the yeast S. cerevisiae and its interactions with various microbial communities and chemical compounds. S. cerevisiae is associated with alterations in microbial community structure and composition, as well as correlations with the chemical Skatole. It is also linked to decreases in certain bacterial populations, such as Bacteroidota, Desulfovibrio, and Streptococcus, and increases in others, including Lysinibacillus, Proteobacteria, and Sphingobacterium. Additionally, S. cerevisiae is cultivated with maltose and peptone, and isolated from the Beijing Beina Chuanglian Biotechnology Research Institute. The CON-DLY and SC-DLY groups are also connected to S. cerevisiae through OTUs.
